subject: SLA template negotiation — flexible uptime tiers and maintenance exception framework
messages:
From: Oliver Park <ops@everleaf.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template: uptime tiers + monthly service credits — initial questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for sending over the initial SLA template earlier today (we reviewed the link in the portal). A couple quick context items from our side: Everleaf is finalizing procurement for a new inference vendor by the end of the month; uptime and predictable monthly economics are the two gating items for procurement.

We have three priority asks up front:
- Can Redwood provide a clear mapping for "critical endpoint" vs "background" services with distinct uptime thresholds? We often need higher guarantees for our real-time APIs.
- We need an explicit monthly reimbursement schedule (not just incident-level credits). What is Redwood's default % or bands for standard uptime tiers?
- Scheduled maintenance: we need a carve-in/notice model. How many hours per month does Redwood exclude by default?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our questions and the services we expect to map to each tier.

Timeline: procurement would like a proposed SLA we can route to legal by Oct 26. Can you send a proposed template and point person we can engage with on redlines?

Thanks,
Oliver Park
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
Everleaf, Inc.
attachments: Everleaf_SLA_Questions.xlsx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Park <ops@everleaf.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime tiers + monthly service credits — initial questions

Hi Oliver — thanks, this is helpful. I'm Naomi (AM for Everleaf); I'll own the SLA thread and work the redlines with your team.

High-level proposal (first draft) — please treat as negotiable:
- Uptime tiers by service class (examples):
  * Tier 1 (real-time API): 99.95% monthly availability
  * Tier 2 (batch/async): 99.5% monthly availability
  * Tier 3 (non-critical): 99.0% monthly availability
- Monthly service reimbursements (bands):
  * Availability >= target: no reimbursement
  * Availability between -0.05% and -0.5%: reimbursement = 2% of monthly invoice
  * Availability between -0.5% and -1.0%: reimbursement = 6% of monthly invoice
  * Availability < -1.0%: reimbursement = 12% of monthly invoice
  (This is intended as a simple sliding scale rather than per-incident credits.)
- Scheduled maintenance carve-in: up to 8 hours/month excluded with 72-hour notice.
- Latency: propose p95 targets per tier (we can map your endpoints). For real-time Tier 1, I recommend p95 <= 250ms as a starting point.

I've attached a PDF of the Redwood SLA template and a short CSV with the uptime table. If you prefer different % bands or a fixed monthly cap on reimbursements we'll discuss tradeoffs — e.g., lower reimbursement caps often require stricter notice and rollback policies.

Next steps: could you review the attached and mark the Tier mapping you'd like applied to each Everleaf endpoint? If you can get that back by Oct 23 I'll loop legal and our contracts team for a redline.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime tiers + monthly service credits — initial questions

Naomi — appreciated. Quick feedback from procurement + legal:
- The 8 hours/month maintenance carve-in is higher than we'd like. Can Redwood consider 4 hours/month (with 72-hour notice) or provide a mechanism to convert excess maintenance into additional notice or lower reimbursement exposure?
- We want a monthly reimbursement cap expressed as a % of the monthly invoice. How would Redwood respond to a 10% cap?
- Latency: we'll accept p95=250ms for Tier 1, but want a measured "burst" exception for predictable traffic spikes (Amazon-style burst windows) so we don't trigger reimbursement during traffic surges beyond our control.

I've attached a short redline that points to where our counsel prefers edits.

Oliver
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
Everleaf, Inc.

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime tiers + monthly service credits — initial questions

Thanks for the clear notes, Oliver — and thanks Julia for being on the thread. I've looped in Marissa (Customer Ops) for operational mapping and Ben (Contracts) for legal/finance framing.

Suggested compromise to move things forward:
- Maintenance carve-in: reduce to 6 hours/month (instead of 8). If Everleaf wants a hard 4 hours we can consider it but it will likely increase the reimbursement percentage in the lower bands; Marissa, could you advise on operational risk at 4 vs 6 hours?
- Monthly reimbursement cap: propose 8% of monthly invoice as a midpoint (we can make this a negotiated cap in the addendum).
- Burst windows: propose we add an "exception buffer" clause — allow up to two burst events/month (up to 30 minutes each) where transient latency spikes are excluded from reimbursement calculation, provided traffic spike is demonstrably external to Redwood's runtime (we'll provide traces).
- Latency SLA: we'll lock p95 <= 250ms for Tier 1; Marissa will provide a mapping template so you can indicate which endpoints map to Tier 1.

I've attached a short agenda for a 30-min call (recommended) and a working copy of the template with the above suggested numbers. If that sounds reasonable, Ben can draft the addendum language and we can route to Everleaf legal for redline.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync Thurs Oct 22 or Fri Oct 23; which works for you?

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Oliver / Julia / Naomi / Marissa — looping in a short legal framing and suggested addendum language. Thanks Naomi for the compromise proposal; below is text we'd propose to include in the SLA addendum. Please note this is intended to be operationally prescriptive and finance-friendly.

--- begin proposed addendum excerpt ---
1) Maintenance carve-out: Redwood will exclude up to 6 hours of scheduled maintenance per calendar month from availability calculations provided Redwood gives at least 72 hours' notice. Any scheduled maintenance exceeding 6 hours in a calendar month will be treated as unplanned downtime for availability calculations unless otherwise agreed in writing.

2) Monthly reimbursement cap: For any monthly period, the total reimbursement payable to the Customer under the Availability bands will not exceed eight percent (8%) of the Customer's total Redwood invoice for that month. This cap is exclusive of any credits agreed for security incidents or data loss.

3) Burst exception buffer: Redwood will exclude up to two (2) transient traffic spike events per month (each up to thirty (30) minutes) from reimbursement calculations if Redwood's diagnostics show the spike originated from the Customer's traffic pattern or upstream third-party events.

4) Latency target and remediation: Tier 1 services will maintain a p95 latency target of 250ms. If p95 exceeds 250ms for two (2) consecutive monthly periods, Redwood will (a) open a remediation plan with defined milestones to return p95 within target within 30 days and (b) provide weekly performance updates until remediation is complete. Credits for latency shortfalls will be held pending remediation outcomes and applied per the Availability bands after review.
--- end proposed addendum excerpt ---

I've attached a draft addendum. If Everleaf accepts these terms we can move to a DocuSign addendum; here's a placeholder link for the proposed doc: https://docusign.example.com/evr-4721

Next steps: Oliver, if you can confirm the 6-hour carve-out and 8% cap (or propose alternate language), we'll finalize the addendum and route to your counsel for redline.

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Head of Legal & Contracts
Redwood Inference
